newsitem.title: CHINA: WTO should compromise for China entry - Rafidah.
newsitem.headline: WTO should compromise for China entry - Rafidah.

text.p: Members of the World Trade Organisation (WTO) should compromise to allow China into the world trade body, Malaysia's Minister of International Trade and Industry Rafidah Aziz said on Wednesday.

"If we want important members of the trading community like China to be in, we must be willing to compromise," Rafidah told a news conference at the current meeting of the International Chamber of Commerce.
Members should allow a transition period for China to meet certain WTO requirements and be "realistic" on the terms and conditions of China's entrance, she said.
"We all hope within this year China will come into the WTO," Rafidah said.

China has been trying to enter the WTO and its predecessor the General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade, for a number of years. Discussions have been largely deadlocked over China's wish to enter the WTO as a developing, as opposed to a developed, country.
